description: As the U.S.’s leading gold company, Newmont also produces copper, lead, silver, and zinc throughout its mines in Africa, Australia, Latin America and the Caribbean, North America, and Papua New Guinea. Its acquisitions of rivals Newcrest and Goldcorp in 2023 and 2019, respectively, each broke the record for the largest deal in the history of the gold mining sector to date. As of April 2025, Newmont confirmed its completion of a divestiture of noncore operations amounting to $3.8 billion in total gross proceeds. These included operations in Ghana, Canada, and Colorado. Newmont was founded in 1921 and has been publicly traded since 1925.

rankings.itemDescription: Colorado-based Newmont was already the world’s largest gold-mining company before it acquired Australian miner Newcrest in 2023. The acquisition helped revenue grow by 58% in 2024, to $18.7 billion. An equally important factor: The average price per ounce at which Newmont sold the gold it mined rose 23% year over year.

rankings.title: Fortune Modern Board 25
rankings.itemDescription: Newmont Corp., the world’s largest gold mining company, has pledged to reach gender parity in leadership roles by 2030 and announced several environmental impact initiatives—although its effort to reduce fresh-water consumption in water-stressed areas by 10% in 2022 fell short. The 12-person board, which has five female directors, is chaired by Gregory Boyce, former CEO of coal company Peabody Energy. Directors have a mix of the operations experience necessary to oversee the manufacturing-intensive mining business, including Julio Quintana, former president and CEO of Tesco Corp., which makes oil drilling equipment; and Emma FitzGerald, former CEO of Puma Energy, an oil company that services emerging markets in Africa, Central America, and Asia. Newmont tapped leaders such as Jane Nelson, a longtime corporate social responsibility advisor for companies like Exxon Mobil and GE, to help it progress on CSR goals, including mining conflict-free gold and increasing the number of local and indigenous employees at its mines. In April, Newmont submitted a reported $19.5 billion bid to buy its competitor Newcrest.

rankings.title: Fortune Modern Board 25
rankings.itemDescription:
Newmont scored high on the Modern Board 25’s rankings for gender equality, nationality dispersion, and board independence. The mining company has received analyst praise for its high dividend yield, strong balance sheet, low debt-to-earnings ratio, and production pipeline longevity. The company expects to deliver approximately 7.5 million ounces of gold by year-end 2022. 

Newmont has implemented several ESG measures into its corporate structure in recent years. The company released its first climate strategy report in 2021, along with annual sustainability and conflict-free-gold reports. Focusing on board diversity, the company reported achieving gender parity for nonexecutive directors in 2020 with the appointment of former American Water Works CEO Susan Story, and reported in 2021 that 70% of its current directors were gender, racially, or ethnically diverse. Including COVID-19 response in its ESG reporting, Newmont announced a $20 million global community support fund to aid communities, governments, and employees through the pandemic; it implemented a vaccine mandate for all employees and third-party contractors in November.

Newmont has six former CEOs on its board, including former Puma Energy CEO Emma FitzGerald and former oilfield services company Tesco CEO Julio Quintana. Newmont CEO Tom Palmer is also a director. Gregory Boyce, former CEO of Peabody Energy and former chairman of the National Mining Association, is chair of Newmont’s board.
